headline: Wired: the recent tech outages may be a sign of more to come
pages: A string of outages last week hit Outlook, Apple, six US banks, United Airlines and even the NSA's classified network. Wired reports there is no evidence of cyberattacks or coordinated AI hacking, and each incident appears to have a routine cause. Microsoft blamed a flawed update, the NSA cited botched patching after October's PHP fixes, and Apple pointed to an internal update. The larger story is pressure. AI tools are finding software bugs at a rapid pace, and attackers use AI to exploit them quickly, so IT teams must test and install patches faster than ever.

Senator Mark Warner said that pace is straining systems not built for it, and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned more instability could come because patches must reach production almost immediately. Researchers also point to years of underinvestment in maintaining digital systems. Why it matters: faster patching can itself cause failures in banking, travel and government networks. Source: Wired.
